rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One derivation of al-ilāh comes from a young camel clinging to its mother: servants cling to God in supplication in every state.
rows.anchor: اشتقاقه من أله الفصيل إذا ولع بأمه والمعنى أن العباد مولهون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People remember only God in severe distress, then credit weak causes after rescue; consistency requires turning to God in ease as well as hardship.
rows.anchor: أن الإنسان إذا وقع في بلاء عظيم وآفة قوية فهنالك ينسى كل شيء إلا الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Goodness and relief are sought from God.
rows.anchor: أن الخير والراحة مطلوب من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Any apparent human benefactor can give only because God creates the impulse to give, so God is the true benefactor to whom people return.
rows.anchor: فإن كان غيره فذلك الغير لا يحسن إلا إذا خلق الله في قلبه داعية الإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A spiritual master describes purifying the heart like working iron: fear softens it, remembrance cleans it, and persistent renunciation empties it of love besides God until divine love and light fill it.
rows.anchor: ثم بعد ذلك شرعت في غسله عن الأوضار والأقذار عشر سنين ثم بعد هذه الأحوال جلست على باب حجرة القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ilāh can derive from fleeing in fear and seeking refuge; God alone protects all creatures from harm.
rows.anchor: أن اشتقاق لفظ الإله من أله الرجل يأله إذا فزع من أمر نزل به فألهه أي أجاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is the true source of blessing, food, and existence, subduing nonexistence through creation; therefore He alone is truly God.
rows.anchor: ولأنه هو المنعم لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God calls sinners His debtors but tells them to flee to Him, since He repays their debts and forgives them.
rows.anchor: عبادي ! أنتم غرمائي بكثرة ذنوبكم ولكن لا تفروا مني بل أقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike kings who close their doors to the poor, God opens His door to them.
rows.anchor: الملوك يغلقون أبوابهم عن الفقراء دون الأغنياء وأنا أفعل ضد ذلك

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says God distributed one mercy among all earthly creatures and reserved ninety-nine mercies for His servants on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: إن لله تعالى مائة رحمة أنزل منها رحمة واحدة بين الجن والإنس والطير والبهائم والهوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says the report was for instruction: divine mercy is an unbounded sea and cannot literally be limited to a number.
rows.anchor: إنه صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما ذكر هذا الكلام على سبيل التفهيم وإلا فبحار الرحمة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: God asks sinners whether they hoped to meet Him; they say they hoped for pardon, and He promises them forgiveness.
rows.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : إن الله عز وجل يقول يوم القيامة للمذنبين

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿUmar describes ninety-nine huge records of sins outweighed by a card bearing the testimony of faith; nothing outweighs remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمر : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : إن الله عز وجل ينشر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Seeing a woman protect her child from heat, the Prophet tells the onlookers that God is more merciful to them than she is to her child.
rows.anchor: فأقبل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى وقف عليهم فأخبروه الخبر فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm are non-Arabic, perhaps Hebrew or Syriac forms later Arabized.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم هذه اللفظة ليست عربية بل عبرانية أو سريانية فإنهم يقولون إلها رحمانا ومرحيانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects foreign origin as an inference from resemblance alone, noting that Arabs identify God as creator and recognize no namesake for Him.
rows.anchor: وهذا بعيد ولا يلزم من المشابهة الحاصلة بين اللغتين الطعن في كون هذه اللفظة عربية أصلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most accept the word as Arabic; those who deny that Allah is a proper name divide between Kufan and Basran derivations.
rows.anchor: وأما الأكثرون فقد سلموا كونها لفظة عربية أما القائلون بأن هذا اللفظ اسم علم لله تعالى

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans derive Allah from ilāh with the article for glorification, then explain loss of hamza and assimilation of the two lām letters.
rows.anchor: قال الكوفيون : أصل هذه اللفظة إلاه

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basrans derive Allah from lāh with the article and cite a poem for the original form.
rows.anchor: وقال البصريون أصله لاه فألحقوا بها الألف واللام فقيل الله وأنشدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted poetic fragment preserves lāh as the underlying form cited for the Basran derivation; the poet is unnamed here.
rows.anchor: كحلفه من أبي رباح … يسمعها

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl says Allah and al-ilāh are specific to God; other uses are either in a construct phrase or indefinite, as in the Israelites’ request for idols.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل : أطبق جميع الخلق على أن قولنا الله مخصوص بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Removing the initial alif from Allah yields lillāh, attested in Qur’anic phrases about God’s armies and treasuries.
rows.anchor: أنك إذا حذفت الألف من قولك الله بقي الباقي على صورة لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further deletion yields lahu and then huwa; the wāw is extra because it drops in the dual and plural forms.
rows.anchor: وإن حذفت عن هذه البقية اللام الأولى بقيت البقية على صورة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Allah encompasses all divine attributes, whereas calling God by a specific name such as al-Raḥmān or al-ʿAlīm identifies one attribute.
rows.anchor: وأما إذا قلت يا الله فقد وصفته بجميع الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The testimony of faith uniquely uses Allah: replacing it with another divine name would not, in Rāzī’s account, take a non-Muslim into Islam.
rows.anchor: أما إذا قال أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله فإنه يخرج من الكفر ويدخل في الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī classifies things as useful and necessary, useful but unnecessary, necessary but harmful, or neither useful nor necessary, with worldly and afterlife examples.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن الأشياء على أربعة أقسام : الذي يكون نافعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Breath is useful and necessary in worldly life, while knowledge of God is necessary for the afterlife; losing it kills the heart and entails endless punishment.
rows.anchor: وإما أن يكون كذلك في الآخرة وهو معرفة الله تعالى فإنها إن زالت عن القلب لحظة واحدة مات القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Money in this world and other kinds of knowledge in the afterlife are useful without being necessary.
rows.anchor: فهو كالمال في الدنيا وكسائر العلوم والمعارف في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly illness, death, poverty, and aging are necessary harms, while the afterlife has no such necessary harm; worldly poverty and afterlife punishment are neither useful nor necessary.
rows.anchor: كالمضار التي لا بد منها في الدنيا : كالأمراض والموت والفقر والهرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Loss of bodily life lasts only a moment, but loss of knowledge of God brings pain that endures forever.
rows.anchor: لكن الموت الأول أسهل من الثاني ؛ لأنه لا يتألم في الموت الأول إلا ساعة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thought functions like breathing: proof preserves balanced faith and knowledge, while reflection expels corrupt doubts from the heart.
rows.anchor: كذلك الفكر له أثران : أحدهما : إيصال نسيم الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recognizing that sensible things are finite and eventually perish helps a person remain safe from harm and reach good outcomes.
rows.anchor: هذه المحسوسات متناهية في مقاديرها منتهية بالآخرة إلى الفناء بعد وجودها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything attained is only a drop from God’s seas of mercy and a speck of His beneficence, revealing the meaning of al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm.
rows.anchor: كل ما وجدته ووصلت إليه فهو قطرة من بحار رحمة الله وذرة من أنوار إحسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human soul begins ignorant, as stated in the Qur’an, and can develop through its sensory, moving, perceptive, and rational powers.
rows.anchor: أما نفسك فلا شك أنها كانت جاهلة في مبدأ الفطرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rational objects are limitless: even endless study at the speed of lightning would yield finite knowledge beside the infinite unknown.
rows.anchor: لكانت المعلومات التي ما عرفها ولم يصل إليها أيضا غير متناهية والمتناهي في جنب غير المتناهي قليل في كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inspecting the body’s four humors, organs, and benefits reveals God’s mercy in creating and guiding people and illuminates al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm.
rows.anchor: أما بدنك فاعلم أنه جوهر مركب من الأخلاط الأربعة فتأمل كيفية تركيبها وتشريحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī’s primary position is that true mercy belongs only to God; even if others are called merciful, God’s mercy is more complete.
rows.anchor: الحق أن الرحمة ليست إلا لله ثم بتقدير أن تكون لغير الله رحمة إلا أن رحمة الله أكمل من رحمة غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God gives without compensation: all other givers seek material or spiritual return, while God is complete in Himself and gains no perfection from giving.
rows.anchor: فكل أحد غير الله فهو إنما يعطي ليأخذ عوضا إلا أن الأعواض أقسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anything contingent exists only through the Necessary Existent, so any mercy coming through another creature is created by God.
rows.anchor: كل من سوى الله فهو ممكن لذاته والممكن لذاته لا يوجد إلا بإيجاد واجب الوجود لذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A human act of mercy occurs only when a decisive motive is present, and God creates that motive in the heart; He is the true merciful agent.
rows.anchor: يمتنع رجحان الفعل على الترك إلا عند حصول داعية جازمة في القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A gift benefits its recipient only through God-given capacities and protection from harm, so God is the real giver and merciful benefactor.
rows.anchor: بل الحق أن خالق تلك الحنطة وذلك البستان هو الله تعالى والممكن من الانتفاع بهما هو الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If creatures also show mercy, God’s gift is better because it humbles the recipient before God rather than before another creature.
rows.anchor: فإذا حصل التواضع بالنسبة إلى حضرة الله فذاك خير من حصول هذه الحالة بالنسبة إلى بعض الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s gifts direct people toward earning eternal happiness, while a creature’s gift usually obliges the recipient to serve that creature’s aims.
rows.anchor: أما غير الله فإنه إذا أنعم عليك بنعمة أمرك بالاشتغال بخدمته والانصراف إلى تحصيل مقصوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Servitude to God is preferable to becoming like a servant of a human benefactor.
rows.anchor: أن المنعم عليه يصير كالعبد للمنعم وعبودية الله أولى من عبودية غير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every need and can fulfill every possible request, unlike human benefactors who may not know or meet a person’s needs.
rows.anchor: أما الحق تعالى فإنه عالم بجميع المعلومات قادر على كل الممكنات فإذا ظهرت بك حاجة عرفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Receiving favor from God is preferable to accepting a human benefactor’s claim of favor.
rows.anchor: الإنعام يوجب المنة وقبول المنة من الحق أفضل من قبولها من الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses first healed his stomach illness after seeking God’s guidance for a plant, but worsened when he later credited the plant itself; God’s name is the world’s antidote.
rows.anchor: لأنك في المرة الأولى ذهبت مني إلى الكلأ فحصل فيه الشفاء وفي المرة الثانية ذهبت منك إلى الكلأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a tale about Rābiʿa, a thief cannot find the door while she sleeps; a voice says that if the beloved sleeps, the Sovereign remains awake.
rows.anchor: ضع القماش واخرج فإن نام الحبيب فالسلطان يقظان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A shepherd says wolves leave his flock alone since the shepherd reconciled himself with God.
rows.anchor: فقال الراعي : من حين اصطلح الراعي مع الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bismillah means I begin in God’s name, with the verb omitted for brevity; its opening position signals ease, lenience, pardon, and beneficence.
rows.anchor: معناه أبدأ باسم الله فأسقط منه قوله أبدأ تخفيفا فإذا قلت بسم الله فكأنك قلت أبدأ باسم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tale says God spared Pharaoh because Moses saw his disbelief while God saw Bismillah written on his palace door; the author infers that inner inscription is more consequential.
rows.anchor: يا موسى لعلك تريد إهلاكه أنت تنظر إلى كفره وأنا أنظر إلى ما كتبه على بابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God named Himself al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm, the author asks rhetorically how He could fail to show mercy.
rows.anchor: سمى نفسه رحمانا رحيما فكيف لا يرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A beggar’s parable asks God to make His gift match His vast door of mercy, and not to deprive worshipers of that mercy.
rows.anchor: إما أن يجعل الباب لائقا بالعطية أو العطية لائقة بالباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm after the name signifying power and exaltedness indicates that mercy is greater and more complete than wrath.
rows.anchor: الله إشارة إلى القهر والقدرة والعلو ثم ذكر عقيبه الرحمن الرحيم وذلك يدل على أن رحمته أكثر وأكمل من قهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a royal mark protects property from enemies, beginning an act with God’s name marks it against Satan, the enemy of obedience.
rows.anchor: إن لطاعتك عدوا وهو الشيطان فإذا شرعت في عمل فاجعل عليه سمتي وقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person should keep company with remembrance of God so as not to be separated from Him in either world.
rows.anchor: اجعل نفسك قرين ذكر الله تعالى حتى لا تبعد عنه في الدارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a report, Abu Bakr refuses to separate Muhammad’s name from God’s on a ring; Gabriel says God likewise honored Abu Bakr’s wish, teaching the value of constant remembrance.
rows.anchor: أما اسم أبي بكر فكتبته أنا لأنه ما رضي أن يفرق اسمك عن اسم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah found rescue using half the formula on the ark, so the author hopes lifelong recitation of the whole formula also brings salvation.
rows.anchor: أن نوحا عليه السلام لما ركب السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon gained worldly and otherworldly kingship through Bismillah, so a servant who recites it may gain both.
rows.anchor: أن سليمان عليه السلام نال مملكة الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that Bilqīs herself says the letter is from Solomon, then identifies Bismillah after opening it; thus Solomon did not place himself before God.
rows.anchor: من كلام بلقيس لا كلام سليمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that Solomon wrote his name on the letter’s outside and began the inside with Bismillah, which Bilqīs read in that order.
rows.anchor: لعل سليمان كتب على عنوان الكتاب إنه من سليمان وفي داخل الكتاب ابتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation says Solomon put his name first because he feared the unbelieving Bilqīs might insult God if His name appeared first.
rows.anchor: أن بلقيس كانت كافرة فخاف سليمان أن تشتم الله إذا نظرت في الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial bāʾ is linked to al-Barr: God’s greatest beneficence is granting believers the vision of Him on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: الباء من بسم مشتق من البر فهو البار على المؤمنين بأنواع الكرامات في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story tells of a Jewish neighbor who accepted Islam because he longed to see God; in a dream he says God forgave him for converting out of that longing.
rows.anchor: أسلمت شوقا إلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letter sīn is linked to God’s name al-Samīʿ, who hears every creature’s prayer from the Throne to beneath the earth.
rows.anchor: وأما السين فهو مشتق من اسمه السميع يسمع دعاء الخلق من العرش إلى ما تحت الثرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tale says Zayd ibn Ḥāritha called on al-Raḥmān when a hypocrite bound him to kill him; successive warnings culminated in Gabriel freeing Zayd and killing the attacker.
rows.anchor: يا رحمن أغثني فسمع المنافق صوتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mīm is associated with God’s dominion extending from the Throne to everything beneath the earth.
rows.anchor: وأما الميم فمعناه أن من العرش إلى ما تحت الثرى ملكه وملكه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: During drought under Solomon, an ant prayed for God’s favor for His creatures, rain came, and Solomon told people to return because another’s prayer had been answered.
rows.anchor: قال السدي : أصاب الناس قحط على عهد سليمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A devotee says he will call on God throughout life, in the grave, at resurrection, while receiving the record, at the scales and bridge, in Paradise, and on seeing God.
rows.anchor: أما قوله الله فاعلموا أيها الناس أني أقول طول حياتي الله فإذا مت أقول الله وإذا سئلت في القبر أقول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three names correspond to three Qur’anic classes: Allah for those foremost in good, al-Raḥmān for the moderate, and al-Raḥīm for the self-wronging.
rows.anchor: فقال أنا الله للسابقين الرحمن للمقتصدين الرحيم للظالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss says Allah gives gifts, al-Raḥmān overlooks the slips of the saints, and al-Raḥīm overlooks their discourtesy.
rows.anchor: الله هو معطي العطاء والرحمن هو المتجاوز عن زلات الأولياء والرحيم هو المتجاوز عن الجفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows hidden faults that would alienate family, spouse, servant, or neighbor, yet conceals them through His generosity.
rows.anchor: وأنا أعلم كل ذمك وأستره بكرمي لتعلم أني إله كريم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises that honoring a paper bearing Bismillah earns the rank of the truthful and lightens one’s parents’ burden even if they were polytheists.
rows.anchor: من رفع قرطاسا من الأرض فيه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم إجلالا له تعالى كتب عند الله من الصديقين

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits instructions to say Bismillah at ablution, intercourse, mounting, and boarding a ship, with good deeds counted through each act and even descendants’ breaths.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that saying Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm while undressing shields people from jinn; Rāzī asks whether it will not also shield them from hell’s guards.
rows.anchor: وعن أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a story, Umar sends Caesar a cap with Bismillah inside; wearing it relieves Caesar’s headache, which returns when he removes it.
rows.anchor: كتب قيصر إلى عمر رضي الله عنه أن بي صداعا لا يسكن فابعث لي دواء

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says invoking God’s name in ablution purifies the whole body, while invoking Him from the heart should purify the heart of unbelief and innovation.
rows.anchor: السابعة عشرة : قال صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says Khalid ibn al-Walīd ate deadly poison after invoking Bismillah and survived by God’s permission, prompting the Magians to accept Islam.
rows.anchor: إنك تدعي الإسلام فأرنا آية لنسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus sees a sinner’s punishment replaced by mercy after the man’s child learns Bismillah; God says He is ashamed to punish below ground while His name is remembered above.
rows.anchor: فاستحييت من عبدي أن أعذبه بناري في بطن الأرض وولده يذكر اسمي على وجه الأرض

rows.speaker: عمرة الفرغانية
rows.claim: ʿUmra al-Farghāniyya explains that menstruating women and the ritually impure may be barred from Qur’an recitation but not from Bismillah, since a beloved is not barred from remembering the beloved.
rows.anchor: لأن التسمية ذكر اسم الحبيب والحبيب لا يمنع من ذكر الحبيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A gloss says al-Raḥīm shows mercy in six fearful stages: the grave, resurrection, scales, record, bridge, and Hell.
rows.anchor: الرحيم هو تعالى رحيم بهم في ستة مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A knower puts Bismillah in his shroud so he can ask God to treat him according to the title of His book.
rows.anchor: بعثت كتابا وجعلت عنوانه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم فعاملني بعنوان كتابك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The formula’s nineteen letters are said to fend off the nineteen guardians of Hell.
rows.anchor: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم تسعة عشر حرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second claim says its nineteen letters expiate sins committed during the nineteen hours left after five daily prayer hours are subtracted from twenty-four.
rows.anchor: خلق الله تعالى الليل والنهار أربعة وعشرين ساعة ثم فرض خمس صلوات في خمس ساعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Tawba lacks Bismillah because it commands fighting; slaughter uses a shorter formula because naming mercy is unsuitable to killing.
rows.anchor: لما كانت سورة التوبة مشتملة على الأمر بالقتال لم يكتب في أولها بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciting the merciful formula seventeen times daily in obligatory prayers indicates that God created people for mercy, favor, and beneficence rather than killing and punishment.
rows.anchor: فلما وفقك لذكر هذه الكلمة في كل يوم سبع عشرة مرة في الصلوات المفروضة دل ذلك على أنه ما خلقك للقتل والعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many names indicate the honor of the named; Fātiḥat al-Kitāb is so called because it opens codices, teaching, recitation, and prayer, or because praise opens speech, or because it was the first sura sent down.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن هذه السورة لها أسماء كثيرة وكثرة الأسماء تدل على شرف المسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called Sūrat al-Ḥamd because its opening word is praise.
rows.anchor: والثاني : سورة الحمد والسبب فيه أن أولها لفظ الحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called the Mother of the Qur’an because its verses encompass the Qur’an’s four central aims: theology, resurrection, prophethood, and divine decree.
rows.anchor: أن أم الشيء أصله والمقصود من كل القرآن تقرير أمور أربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reason for calling it the Mother of the Book is that all revelation comprises praise, worshipful service, and requests for unveiling; the sura includes each in that order.
rows.anchor: أن حاصل جميع الكتب الإلهية يرجع إلى أمور ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reason is that all knowledge concerns either divine lordship or human servitude: the opening praises God’s mastery, while the remainder shows the servant’s dependence on His aid and guidance.
rows.anchor: معرفة عزة الربوبية أو معرفة ذلة العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth reason is that the sura gathers theology, religious duties, and spiritual purification: praise and lordship establish divine existence and attributes, worship presents duties, and guidance seeks unveiling.
rows.anchor: أن العلوم البشرية إما علم ذات الله وصفاته وأفعاله وهو علم الأصول وإما علم أحكام الله تعالى وتكاليفه وهو علم الفروع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the mystical reading, guidance brings light to the heart, the blessed become polished mirrors reflecting sanctity, and the final plea seeks protection from desire and doubt.
rows.anchor: حصول هداية النور في القلب

rows.speaker: ابن دريد
rows.claim: Ibn Durayd says umm can mean a banner; the Fātiḥa is the believers’ rallying point as a banner is an army’s, while earth is called mother because all return to it and umm can mean a destination.
rows.anchor: الأم في كلام العرب الراية التي ينصبها العسكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of al-sabʿ al-mathānī is that half the sura is the servant’s praise and half God’s gift to the servant.
rows.anchor: نصفها ثناء العبد للرب ونصفها عطاء الرب للعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that it is repeated in every prayer cycle.
rows.anchor: سميت مثاني لأنها تثنى في كل ركعة من الصلاة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says no comparable sura occurs in the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, or Qur’an, and identifies it as the seven oft-repeated verses and the great Qur’an.
rows.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام صلى الله عليه وسلم : والذي نفسي بيده ما أنزل في التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation says each of its seven verses equals the recitation of seven portions of the Qur’an, so reciting it earns the reward of reciting all of it.
rows.anchor: سميت مثاني لأنها سبع آيات كل آية تعدل قراءتها قراءة سبع من القرآن

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: Gabriel says the seven verses overlay Hell’s seven gates, so reciters pass them safely; he had feared punishment before the Fātiḥa was revealed.
rows.anchor: روي أن جبريل عليه السلام قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called the oft-repeated because it is recited in prayer and then followed by another sura.
rows.anchor: لأنها تقرأ في الصلاة ثم إنها تثنى بسورة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes mathānī as praises and commendations of God.
rows.anchor: سميت مثاني لأنها أثنية على الله تعالى ومدائح له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final explanation says God revealed the sura twice, which is why it is called oft-repeated.
rows.anchor: سميت مثاني لأن الله أنزلها مرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called the Foundation because it is the first sura, contains the noblest aims, and is indispensable to prayer, the greatest worship after faith.
rows.anchor: أنها أول سورة من القرآن فهي كالأساس

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet calls the Fātiḥa healing from every poison; a companion’s recitation cured an epileptic, and the Prophet also calls it healing from every disease.
rows.anchor: أبي سعيد الخدري قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī explains the healing spiritually and physically: since unbelief is called a disease, the sura’s theology, duties, and spiritual unveilings heal all three domains.
rows.anchor: والدليل عليه أنه تعالى سمى الكفر مرضا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: It is called prayer because God says He divided the prayer between Himself and His servant in two halves, meaning this sura.
rows.anchor: الاسم التاسع : الصلاة قال عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says whoever is occupied with remembering God rather than asking receives more than those who ask; Abraham models praise followed by requests.
rows.anchor: روي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حكى عن رب العزة سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the sura moves from praise to worship to a request for guidance, it teaches that religious guidance is the highest aim and the garden of knowledge surpasses the garden of pleasure.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن أكمل المطالب هو الهداية في الدين وهو أيضا يدل على أن جنة المعرفة خير من جنة النعيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called the Sura of Gratitude because it praises God for His favor, generosity, and beneficence.
rows.anchor: سورة الشكر وذلك لأنها ثناء على الله بالفضل والكرم والإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called the Sura of Supplication because it includes the request for the straight path.
rows.anchor: سورة الدعاء لاشتمالها على قوله

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Fātiḥa descended in Mecca from a treasure beneath the Throne; al-Thaʿlabī says most scholars agree.
rows.anchor: روى الثعلبي بإسناده عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: عمرو بن شرحبيل
rows.claim: ʿAmr ibn Shurayḥil says the first revelation was al-Ḥamd lillāh; after Muhammad confided his fear to Khadīja and consulted Waraqa, Gabriel instructed him to recite Bismillah and the Fātiḥa.
rows.anchor: وروى أيضا بإسناده عن عمرو بن شرحبيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet recited Bismillah and Quraysh cursed him.
rows.anchor: وبإسناده عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says it descended in Medina, but Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl rejects this as a lapse against scholarly consensus.
rows.anchor: روى الثعلبي بإسناده عن مجاهد أنه قال

rows.speaker: حسين بن الفضل
rows.claim: Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl argues that the Meccan Sūrat al-Ḥijr already refers to the seven oft-repeated verses and that it is implausible for the Prophet to live in Mecca over a decade without the Fātiḥa.
rows.anchor: أن سورة الحجر مكية بالاتفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view holds that the sura descended once in Mecca and again in Medina, its double revelation explaining its honorific name al-mathānī.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة نزلت بمكة مرة وبالمدينة مرة أخرى

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports from the Prophet that the Fātiḥa heals poison.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
rows.claim: Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Yamān reports that a child’s recitation of al-Ḥamd lillāh during a destined calamity leads God to lift it for forty years.
rows.anchor: وعن حذيفة بن اليمان قال

rows.speaker: الحسين
rows.claim: Al-Ḥusayn says knowledge flowed from 104 heavenly books through the four major books and the Qur’an until it was concentrated in the Fātiḥa, whose interpretation equals knowledge of all revelation.
rows.anchor: أنزل الله تعالى مائة وأربعة كتب من السماء فأودع علوم المائة في الأربعة وهي التوراة والإنجيل والزبور والفرقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī explains that the Fātiḥa contains all divine aims because it fully treats theology, religious practice, and spiritual unveiling.
rows.anchor: والسبب فيه أن المقصود من جميع الكتب الإلهية علم الأصول والفروع والمكاشفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura omits seven letters associated with torment: thāʾ with ruin, jīm with Hell, khāʾ with disgrace, zāy and shīn with breath, the tree or misery, ẓāʾ with shade and blazing fire, and fāʾ with separation or falsehood.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الحروف السبعة مشعرة بالعذاب فالثاء تدل على الويل والثبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers that, although all letters can occur in words about punishment, these seven omitted initials correspond to Hell’s seven gates; understanding the sura protects readers from them.
rows.anchor: والله تعالى أسقط سبعة من الحروف من هذه السورة وهي أوائل ألفاظ دالة على العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase al-ḥamdu lillāh raises questions about God’s existence and right to praise; Rabb al-ʿālamīn answers the first, while al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm, and Mālik yawm al-dīn answer the second.
rows.anchor: فأجاب عن السؤال الأول بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge of God’s existence is theoretical, not immediate; the world of heavens, earth, seas, minerals, plants, and animals needs a governing, originating, nurturing, and sustaining cause.
rows.anchor: هذا العالم المحسوس بما فيه من السموات والأرضين والجبال والبحار والمعادن والنبات والحيوان محتاج إلى مدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿālamīn includes everything besides God, which depends on Him for existence and continuance; every indivisible particle and individual accident proves the wise, powerful God.
rows.anchor: أن العالمين إشارة إلى كل ما سوى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī prefers Rabb al-ʿālamīn to Creator of the worlds because sustaining creatures after their beginning is disputed, and the phrase stresses their dependence on God at every moment.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يستغني عنه لا في حال حدوثه ولا في حال بقائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the Mother of the Qur’an, the Fātiḥa is the source from which other suras branch; every being besides God is evidence of His divinity.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مسماة بأم القرآن فوجب كونها كالأصل والمعدن وأن يكون غيرها كالجداول المتشعبة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Anʿām’s praise for creating the heavens, earth, darkness, and light is one subset of Rabb al-ʿālamīn; dependence on God for preservation entails dependence for origination.
rows.anchor: لأن لفظ العالم يتناول كل ما سوى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kahf’s praise for the revealed Book concerns spiritual nurture through knowledge and unveiling, one kind of the Fātiḥa’s universal nurturing.
rows.anchor: والمقصود منه تربية الأرواح بالمعارف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saba’s statement that everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God is another subset within the universal lordship named in the Fātiḥa.
rows.anchor: الأشياء الحاصلة في السماوات والأرض له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāṭir describes bringing the heavens and earth into existence, distinct from creation as determination yet also included within Rabb al-ʿālamīn.
rows.anchor: والخلق هو التقدير والمذكور في هذه السورة كونه فاطرا لها ومحدثا لذواتها
